artifacts.summary: Six-phase plan re-basing the frame-class Galois layer on Mathlib.Order.Concept and tidying the correspondence modules, 5.5 hours across three dependency waves.

memory_candidates.content: When re-basing a hand-rolled Galois/adjunction layer onto Mathlib, prefer the polarity API in Mathlib.Order.Concept (upperPolar/lowerPolar/Order.IsExtent) over deriving everything from an explicit GaloisConnection. The GaloisConnection route forces one side through OrderDual (e.g. mod_th_mod via .dual.u_l_u_eq_u, plus simp cleanup), while Concept supplies dual-free direct lemmas: lowerPolar_upperPolar_lowerPolar, upperPolar_lowerPolar_upperPolar, lowerPolar_union (a plain @[simp] lemma, not GaloisConnection.l_sup), lowerPolar_empty. Still declare the GaloisConnection as a named theorem for discoverability, but derive nothing from it. Two further gotchas: defining the closure predicate as Order.IsExtent changes it from a fixed-point equation to a range membership -- equivalent by Order.isExtent_iff but NOT defeq, so audit consumers and ship a one-line `iff` compat lemma; and importing a Mathlib module for its lemmas also injects its @[simp] lemmas into the default simp set for every downstream module, which is a whole-tree build risk, not a single-module one.
